summary: The cut is clean and the first strip is stable, but the hand-lift on "secret" snaps up with no anticipation and then freezes with the hand at or above the top edge of the frame.

faults.what: The free arm goes from forearm low across the belly with fingers pointing down (12.00) to the hand up at face height (12.06) and above the head line (12.10). That is about two frames for a large arc, so it reads as a snap rather than a lift.
faults.fix: Add 3-4 in-between frames on the rise, or ease the arm into the lift. A small preparatory dip before it would also help.

faults.what: From 11.76 to 12.00 the hand drifts down across the torso with no anticipation. At 11.93-12.00 the fingers hang and point at the floor, then the arm whips up. The move gives no cue for the gesture, so the lift feels unmotivated.
faults.fix: Hold the hand low briefly, or add a small wind-up. Avoid the fingers-down dangle before the lift.

faults.what: From 12.13 to 12.30 the raised hand is at or past the top edge of the crop, so the fist is cut off. The key gesture, the hand beside the face, is not fully readable and the blade of grass cannot be seen.
faults.fix: Reframe or tilt down slightly so the hand and the face fit in frame, or lower the hand to cheek height.

faults.what: From 12.13 to 12.30 the raised arm is almost frozen in one pose, with a closed fist and no finger detail. The cup arm and torso are also static throughout, so the gesture feels stiff and the secret idea is not conveyed.
faults.fix: Open the fingers into a small pinch or hold to show the blade. Add slight settle and overshoot on arrival, plus a small head or eye reaction.
